newsitem.title: UK: BA dips amid concern over U.S. alliance.
newsitem.headline: BA dips amid concern over U.S. alliance.

text.p: Shares in British Airways Plc lost height in early trading on Wednesday as comments from rival airline operator Richard Branson raised concerns about BA's planned alliance with American Airlines, dealers said.
BA shares were down 6p at 723 by 0737 GMT, even as the FTSE 100 rose 16.4 points to a record 4,756.0.

Speaking on CNN's Moneyline programme, Branson said he was confident that antitrust bodies would ultimately prevent BA's proposed transatlantic alliance, adding that other airlines would consider forming a rival alliance if the deal went through.
Branson -- whose diverse interests include Virgin Atlantic -- and other airline executives were due to testify to a Congressional hearing on airline regulation later on Wednesday.

"I think that public opinion is beginning to move quite strongly against British Airways and American Airlines getting together," Branson said. "So we're beginning to become more and more hopeful that we can see it stopped."

Dealers said Branson's comments had sent BA shares lower, even though they were probably to be expected from the entrepreneurial figure, who has a long-standing antagonistic relationship with the British flag-carrier.
"The potential scuppering of the deal is what's sent BA lower," said one.

BA chairman Sir Colin Marshall said on Wednesday he had no idea when the proposed alliance, first announced a year ago, may be approved. He said BA may abandon the link-up if regulatory demands became too great.
